note: Whole-sector UK technology tables across five sectors and every end use. Broadest source held.

UKTM investment costs across eight sectors and 390 technologies, plus a literature survey. Broad in coverage but narrow in parameters - essentially capex alone. Ranked above the single-technology briefs on breadth and below UKERC, which carries energy, emissions and adoption as well.

Assessed, cross-sector and the most recent broad source held. Ranked below UKERC and Bataille only because its parameters barely overlap theirs: it gives abatement costs and reduction potentials, not capex and efficiencies, so it rarely competes for the same cell.
CHP catalogue covering five prime movers, size-resolved. Recent.
Biomass CHP catalogue covering boilers, gasifiers and four prime movers.

Iron and steel only, but 16 technologies across every step of the sector - blast furnace, smelting reduction, direct reduction, EAF, BOF, coking, sintering, pelletisation - with per-tonne material and energy flows as well as costs. Ranked above LBNL 2021 and ETSAP I01 on that breadth and below the cross-industry catalogues; LBNL and I01 moved down one place to make room. Its costs come in two denominations (EUR2010 for the blast furnace and COREX columns, USD2000 for everything else) and the brief gives no way to reconcile them.

Cement only, but 16 technologies covering every clinker kiln type, the grate cooler, both state-of-the-art grinding mills and two alternative binders, with thermal energy, capacity, air flow, costs and the full emissions block. Tied with ETSAP I02 at 6: the two sector briefs are the same kind of source and cover disjoint sectors, so they never compete for the same cell. Costs come in EUR2010 and EUR2007, and the brief states the IEA costs per tonne of cement while its own summary table heads them per tonne of clinker - see the meta file.

Pulp and paper only, but nine products with a full per-tonne energy breakdown and eight kraft-mill energy investment options. Tied with ETSAP I02 and I03 at 6 - same kind of source, disjoint sectors. The most recent ETSAP brief held. Two cautions: the energy block is Swedish mill averages, not world averages, and the investment cost carries no currency year at all.

Aluminium only; ten technologies across electrolysis, alumina refining, anode production, casting and secondary melting. Tied with ETSAP I02, I03 and I07 at 6. Its strength is the emissions block - seven pollutants over five cell configurations, which nothing else held comes close to. Its weakness is cost: two cost rows only, with no currency year stated anywhere in the brief, and an operating cost that explicitly EXCLUDES fuel in the one industry where power is the dominant cost.
Boiler electrification only. Recent but narrow.
